sugestoes.texto: In sync mode the helper returns the raw `fetch` `Response`, but callers such as zoho-bigin/zohocrm/hubspot/googlecalendar expect axios-shaped or SDK-shaped objects and access `.data`/`.expiresIn`. This causes runtime failures or NaN expiry values whenever credential sync is turned on.

The `userId` argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is given `credentialId`, the credential's primary key, instead of the Cal.com user's id. The credential-sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong `calcomUserId` and cannot return the correct tokens for that user.

When the token response lacks a `refresh_token`, the helper silently substitutes the literal placeholder `"refresh_token"`. Callers then store that placeholder in the database, masking the missing token and breaking any later local refresh if the sync endpoint is unavailable.

The handler reads an existing credential with `findFirst` and then decides whether to `create` or `update`, but the `Credential` table has no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`. Concurrent webhook requests can both pass the `findFirst` check and insert duplicate credentials for the same user and app.

The newly-added refresh fetch obtains a fresh access token and writes it to the database, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still constructed with the stale `credentialKey.access_token`. The refreshed token is persisted but never used for the connection that is returned to callers.

The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and is vulnerable to timing analysis. An attacker who can measure response times could brute-force the secret character-by-character.

The outbound request to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` uses `fetch` with no timeout. If the endpoint is slow or unresponsive, every calendar/video token refresh awaits indefinitely, blocking the request and the underlying Next.js worker.

WHAT: The Google Calendar refresh stores the value returned by `parseRefreshTokenResponse` directly as the credential `key`, but that helper returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credential data. WHY: The next time the credential is loaded from the database, the OAuth token fields will be nested under a `data` property and Google Calendar API calls will fail because `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and `expiry_date` are not at the top level. HOW: Extract `parsedKey.data` before writing to the database.

WHAT: The newly added Salesforce token refresh validates the HTTP response by comparing `response.statusText` to the literal string `"OK"`. WHY: HTTP status text is not guaranteed to be `"OK"` (HTTP/2 responses often omit it, and proxies or servers may send custom text), so valid token responses can be rejected and error responses can be mishandled. HOW: Check `!response.ok` or `response.status !== 200` and inspect the JSON body for provider errors.

WHAT: The credential-sync refresh request sends `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no authentication header or signature. WHY: The endpoint has no way to verify the request came from Cal.com, so any party that can reach the endpoint can trigger credential refresh operations or probe user/app mappings. HOW: Include `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (or a dedicated sync secret) in an `Authorization` header or signed request body and validate it on the endpoint.

WHAT: The new Salesforce token refresh path directly calls `login.salesforce.com` and does not route through the `refreshOAuthTokens` helper that every other changed OAuth app uses. WHY: The PR's credential-sync feature is bypassed for Salesforce, so self-hosters cannot make their app store the source of truth for Salesforce credentials. HOW: Wrap the Salesforce refresh fetch in `refreshOAuthTokens` with `appSlug: "salesforce"` and `credential.userId`, like the other apps.

WHAT: The webhook handler reads the secret from `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` without lowercasing the configured header name. WHY: Node.js lowercases all incoming HTTP header keys, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` contains uppercase letters the lookup returns `undefined` and valid webhook requests are rejected with 403. HOW: Normalize the configured name before indexing `req.headers`.

The newly-added refresh fetch obtains a fresh access token and writes it to the database, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still constructed with the stale `credentialKey.access_token`. The refreshed token is persisted but never used for the connection that is returned to callers.

WHAT: The Google Calendar refresh stores the value returned by `parseRefreshTokenResponse` directly as the credential `key`, but that helper returns a Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credential data. WHY: The next time the credential is loaded from the database, the OAuth token fields will be nested under a `data` property and Google Calendar API calls will fail because `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and `expiry_date` are not at the top level. HOW: Extract `parsedKey.data` before writing to the database.

Sending the credential-sync refresh request without an `Authorization` header or signature lets anyone who can reach `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` trigger refreshes or probe user/app mappings. Add `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` as a bearer token in the request headers and validate it on the endpoint.

Returning the raw `fetch` `Response` from sync mode hands callers a `Response` object instead of the axios-shaped payload they expect, so accesses to `.data` or `.expiresIn` throw or produce `NaN` expiry values when credential sync is enabled. Parse the response with `response.json()` before returning it.

Using `!==` to compare the webhook secret short-circuits at the first mismatch and leaks timing information, letting an attacker brute-force the secret byte-by-byte. Replace the comparison with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` after reading the header into a `Buffer`.

A `fetch` without a timeout to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` can hang indefinitely when the endpoint is slow, blocking every token refresh and the Next.js worker handling it. Add an `AbortController` with a fixed timeout and pass its signal to the `fetch` call.

Indexing `req.headers` with the raw `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` value fails when the name contains uppercase characters because Node.js lowercases incoming header keys. Normalize the configured header name with `.toLowerCase()` before looking it up.

issues.descricao: The new app-credential webhook checks its shared secret with a plain !== string comparison instead of a constant-time comparison, leaking timing information about the secret.

comentarios.texto: Direct !== comparison of webhook secret leaks via timing attack. Use constant-time comparison (e.g., crypto.timingSafeEqual on hashed/buffered values with length check) instead of `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

The webhook authenticates a secret using direct string inequality, which is not constant-time and can leak information about the secret through comparison timing. Compare fixed-length representations using a constant-time primitive (such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), handling absent or malformed headers safely, instead of comparing the secret strings directly.

The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret via response timing (timing attack). An attacker can iteratively recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and then forge requests that create/update arbitrary user credential keys (decrypted with the AES key) via this endpoint. Use a constant-time comparison, e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, guarding for length mismatch first.

issues.descricao: The webhook parses the body with zod .parse and decrypts/JSON-parses the keys without error handling, so invalid payloads produce 500 errors instead of 400 responses.
issues.textoGolden: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zod parse, symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse throw unhandled (no try/catch) with no method guard. WHY: Invalid body/keys or GET request crashes handler with 500 and leaks stack, instead of 400/405. HOW: Wrap parse/decrypt in try/catch returning 400 and restrict to POST.

schema .parse plus symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse throw unhandled (ZodError, decrypt error, SyntaxError) on invalid body or tampered keys, crashing webhook with 500. Use safeParse and try/catch with 400 responses.

issues.descricao: The webhook's non-atomic findFirst-then-create lets concurrent deliveries for the same user and app insert duplicate credential rows.

comentarios.texto: The webhook performs a non-atomic findFirst followed by create when no credential exists. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no row and insert duplicates because Credential has no unique userId/appId constraint; subsequent findFirst updates only one duplicate, leaving competing credentials stale. Serialize the lookup/create operation for each user/app pair or introduce an appropriate uniqueness constraint and atomic upsert.

issues.descricao: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when the refresh response omits a refresh token, so the stored credential gets an invalid refresh token and later refreshes fail.
issues.textoGolden: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: The parser fabricates the literal refresh token "refresh_token" whenever a successful response omits refresh_token, including when synchronization is disabled. Office365's response schema explicitly permits that omission, and its caller merges parsed data over existing credentials, replacing the valid saved refresh token with this invalid value and breaking the next refresh. Leave the property absent so the existing token survives the merge.

When a refresh response omits refresh_token, this helper manufactures the hardcoded credential "refresh_token". Callers such as Office365 merge this into stored credentials, overwriting the valid existing refresh token and causing subsequent provider refreshes to use a predictable invalid token. Leave the field absent and preserve the existing credential when omission is allowed by the provider, or reject the response when a refresh token is required; do not substitute a literal authentication token.

WHAT: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal string "refresh_token". WHY: Stores bogus refresh token in DB, breaking all future refreshes and masking provider errors. HOW: Preserve existing credential refresh_token or throw instead of injecting placeholder.

issues.descricao: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys from z.string().toString(), which produce a literal key rather than a wildcard, so the sync-mode schema does not validate or keep expiry and other token fields as intended.
issues.textoGolden: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

comentarios.texto: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to a fixed string key such as "ZodString", so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a literal numeric property with that name. Every synced token response fails validation and throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `z.object({access_token: z.string()}).passthrough()` instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property named "[object Object]", so safeParse always fails in credential-sync mode and the function throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` on an object with access_token and optional numeric expiry fields instead.

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a literal string like "ZodString" and not to a wildcard. The schema therefore requires a numeric property with that nonsense name and never matches real token responses. In sync mode every refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Use `.passthrough()` and a real expiry check instead.

issues.descricao: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers expect their provider-specific shapes (res.data, axios .data, HubspotToken), so token refresh breaks for Google, Zoho and HubSpot when credential sharing is on.
issues.textoGolden: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of a parsed token payload, yet several callers treat the result as an already-parsed token object.
WHY: Callers such as hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and googlecalendar (`res?.data`) read `.data`/token fields off the return value; a `Response` has neither, so the sync path yields `undefined`/`NaN` or throws a TypeError — the feature's primary code path is broken for those apps.
HOW: Parse the response (e.g. `const data = await response.json(); return data;`) before returning, or make every caller await the appropriate response handler.

In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response (no `.data`), but the google caller reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError swallowed by the catch, so the token is never refreshed.

`res?.data` assumes the value returned by refreshOAuthTokens has a `.data` field (true for the `fetchTokens.res` branch), but when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data`. Then `token.access_token` throws. Either parse the shared-mode Response here or have refreshOAuthTokens return a normalized `{ data }` shape.

issues.descricao: Google Calendar persists the safeParse result object instead of its data as the credential key, corrupting the stored credential so later reads fail.
issues.textoGolden: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result {success,data}, not the parsed key. Storing it directly as `key` writes the wrapper to the credential. Unwrap like other callers: check .success and use .data.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse result {success,data}, but call site stores that wrapper as credential `key` (previously googleCredentialSchema.parse() returned the plain object). Store `key.data` / handle wrapper, otherwise persisted credential becomes {success,data} shape and subsequent credential reads fail.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns SafeParse wrapper {success,data} but code stores the whole wrapper as credential.key. Office365calendar in same PR unwraps via .data. Persisted credential will be {success,data} instead of tokens, so next load fails validation. Unwrap to .data after success check.

issues.descricao: After switching to parseRefreshTokenResponse, the tokenResponse.success check in Office365 refreshAccessToken is dead code and the previous error logging was dropped.

comentarios.texto: parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws when parsing fails, so the `tokenResponse.success` check on the next line is dead code and the previous error logging was removed. A failed refresh now throws out of refreshAccessToken instead of keeping the old credentials. Catch the error or restore the previous handling.

issues.descricao: Salesforce getClient now refreshes the OAuth token and writes the credential on every service construction, adding a network round trip and DB write even when the access token is valid.

comentarios.texto: getClient now unconditionally exchanges the Salesforce refresh token on every service construction, even when the saved access token is valid. Each constructor invocation adds a blocking OAuth network round trip and credential database write before any Salesforce operation, replacing jsforce's existing on-demand refresh behavior. Keep refresh on demand or guard the exchange with a token-expiration check.

issues.descricao: The new Salesforce token refresh uses prisma without importing it, so the code fails type checking and throws a ReferenceError at runtime.

comentarios.texto: The new credential update references prisma without importing or declaring it; searching this file finds only the new usage. This fails TypeScript checking and raises ReferenceError after a successful token exchange at runtime. Import prisma from @calcom/prisma before using it.

issues.descricao: Zoho Bigin passes the credential id instead of the user id to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId.
issues.textoGolden: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The 3rd argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (= `credential.id`, line 53), but the function's parameter is `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`).
WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the sync endpoint is sent `calcomUserId: <credential id>` instead of the user id, so Bigin credentials are synced against the wrong/non-existent user (all other apps correctly pass `credential.userId`).
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` instead of `credentialId` as the third argument.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether sharing runs), but this call passes `credentialId`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential row id as the user id and shared credentials are fetched/updated for the wrong identity. Pass `credential.userId` here.

refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` (declared in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 3 and used as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id, line 53) instead of the user id. When credential sharing is enabled the customer's sync endpoint receives a credential id labelled as calcomUserId and cannot resolve the correct Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` (the BiginToken/credential payload carries it) or plumb the user id through refreshAccessToken.

issues.descricao: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok when refreshing the token, which can misclassify successful responses, and then ignores the refreshed token.
issues.textoGolden: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Checks response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok and builds jsforce.Connection from stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url ignoring accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: Refresh never takes effect (old token reused) and valid refreshes can throw on runtimes where statusText is empty. HOW: Check !response.ok and use parsed access_token/instance_url for connection and DB update.

issues.descricao: After refreshing the Salesforce token, jsforce.Connection is created with the stale access_token and instance_url instead of the newly refreshed values.
issues.textoGolden: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new block fetches and persists a fresh access token (`accessTokenParsed.data`) but then creates the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-refreshed token.
WHY: The refreshed token is written to the DB but never used for the connection; if the old token was expired, jsforce must refresh again (extra round trip) or fail, and the DB/connection state diverge.
HOW: Pass the new access token (`accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) to the `jsforce.Connection`.

issues.descricao: The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: When the use-table-widget-visualization feature flag is enabled, the table branch renders TableWidgetVisualization with empty columns=[] and empty tableData instead of the actual result data. WHY: Users with the flag enabled will see an empty table even though query results exist. HOW: Pass the real columns derived from fields, result.data, and result.meta into TableWidgetVisualization instead of the hardcoded empty values.

WHAT: validate_timestamp and validate_age check for the presence of the other field using truthiness (self.initial_data.get('age')), so a report containing timestamp=0 and age=0 passes mutual-exclusivity validation. WHY: Both specs require age and timestamp to be mutually exclusive; falsy-but-present values bypass the check. HOW: Use membership tests ('age' in self.initial_data and 'timestamp' in self.initial_data) instead of truthiness.

WHAT: fetch_error_details reads event timestamps from raw nodestore data as data.get('timestamp', 0.0), but production nodestore stores event timestamps as ISO 8601 strings, not floats. WHY: gen_request_data later compares error event timestamps against numeric replay event timestamps, which raises TypeError when a string is compared to a number. HOW: Convert the nodestore timestamp string to a numeric timestamp (e.g., using datetime.fromisoformat(...).timestamp()) before constructing ErrorEvent, and handle the case where the conversion fails.

WHAT: The endpoint passes the user's `field` query params directly to process_raw_response, so a client that does not request `error_ids` gets an empty error ID list and error context is silently skipped. WHY: The new error-context feature depends on `error_ids` from the replay record, but the fieldset filtering removes it whenever the caller limits the response fields. HOW: Always include `error_ids` in the field list before calling process_raw_response.

WHAT: fetch_error_details pairs error IDs with nodestore payloads by zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()`, but nodestore.get_multi can return values in a different order than the requested IDs when some are cache hits. WHY: This can attach the wrong title/message/timestamp to a replay error ID, corrupting the chronological error context sent to the summarizer. HOW: Look up each payload by its node_id instead of relying on ordering.

issues.descricao: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
issues.textoGolden: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

comentarios.texto: The timestamp/age validators test truthiness and make both fields optional instead of enforcing exactly one field. Reports with both age=0 and timestamp=0, or with neither field, pass validation despite violating the stated mutually exclusive report formats. Enforce field presence and exclusivity in object-level validate using key membership rather than truthiness.

Check key presence rather than truthiness when enforcing age/timestamp mutual exclusion. Both fields permit 0, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 passes both validators even though both fields are present; a zero-valued counterpart also bypasses the corresponding check. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or object-level validation) and add zero-value tests.

Check field presence rather than truthiness when enforcing timestamp/age exclusivity. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes both validators, despite the declared constraint that they must not coexist; with only one zero value, validation is also asymmetric. Use membership checks on initial_data (or object-level validation) and add zero-value mixed-field tests.

issues.descricao: The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.

comentarios.texto: The new validation-failure warning logs `raw_report`, the full unvalidated report object supplied by the caller. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated (permission_classes = (), @csrf_exempt), so the payload is attacker-controlled, and browser report bodies routinely carry sensitive values (CSP blocked-uri/document-uri/script-sample, sourceFile, plus the full user_agent). Logging the raw payload on every validation failure writes potentially sensitive data into application logs; log only the report `type` (or a sanitized/redacted subset) instead of the entire raw object.

Do not attach the complete raw report to the validation warning. Browser reports contain page URLs (potentially including tokens or personal data in query strings) and arbitrary body contents. Any invalid field now causes that entire payload to be emitted at warning level, exposing it in operational logs even where the existing info-level request logging is filtered out. Log the failed field names/report type or a redacted diagnostic instead.

issues.descricao: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids positionally with nodestore get_multi values, but get_multi does not preserve input order (cached items are appended last) and drops missing nodes, so error details get attached to the wrong error IDs.
issues.textoGolden: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() instead of mapping by node_id, misaligning ids to payloads and dropping/mismatching on missing keys. WHY: assigns wrong title/message/timestamp to wrong error id and yields incorrect Seer logs. HOW: look up each node_id in the get_multi dict (e.g. dict keyed by node_id) and preserve error_ids order.

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` values preserve input order and that all keys exist. Dict values give no such guarantee; missing keys shorten/misalign the zip, attaching the wrong event payload to the wrong error_id. Lookup per-id: iterate node_ids/error_ids and do `events.get(node_id)` instead of zipping with `.values()`.

fetch_error_details pairs IDs to payloads with zip(error_ids, events.values()) where events is dict from nodestore get_multi. Values order need not match IDs and missing keys misalign, attaching wrong title/message to wrong error. Look up per node_id instead.

issues.descricao: The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

comentarios.texto: The new Snuba replay lookup executes even when enable_error_context=false. Every opt-out summary request incurs an unnecessary database round trip and can now fail on Snuba availability even though it only needs recording storage. Evaluate the flag first and perform the replay lookup only when error context is enabled.

issues.descricao: With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `use-table-widget-visualization` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, hardcoding empty rows and no columns instead of the actual query result. WHY: when the feature flag is enabled for an org, every table widget renders an empty table and silently drops `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns`, a functional regression for all dashboard table widgets. HOW: build `columns`/`tableData` from the existing `result` (and `widget.queries[i].fields`/`fieldAliases`) rather than the empty placeholder objects.

In the new feature-flagged branch, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty props: columns={[]} (an empty array, which is truthy for the `columns ?? fallback` logic, so no columns are derived) and tableData={data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}. All the real result data computed above (result.data, result.meta, fields, fieldAliases, eventView) is discarded, so any organization with 'use-table-widget-visualization' enabled gets an empty table instead of the query results. Pass the actual result data/columns into the visualization (or keep the old StyledSimpleTableChart) until the widget is properly wired.

With the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty data/meta instead of result.data and result.meta. Every table widget therefore renders empty for orgs with the flag. Fix: pass tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}} and build columns from the fields.

issues.descricao: The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.

comentarios.texto: The documented custom-renderer contract says fallback runs when the callback returns undefined, but `if (cell)` also falls back for valid ReactNode results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null`. A caller trying to render zero or deliberately suppress a cell instead gets the default field rendering. Check `cell !== undefined` here and in the head-cell renderer so the implementation honors the advertised contract.

Use `cell !== undefined` instead of `if (cell)` to select the custom renderer result, and apply the same correction to the header renderer. The API documents undefined as the fallback sentinel, but valid ReactNode results such as numeric 0, an empty string, or null are falsy. A custom renderer returning 0 or intentionally hiding a cell with null therefore unexpectedly renders the default value instead.

issues.descricao: The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

comentarios.texto: The new attribute query key omits the organization even though its query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Switching organizations with identical project selections such as all projects and the same date range reuses the singleton query client's prior organization's attribute metadata, including while the new request refetches. Include organization.slug or organization.id in the query key.

Include the organization slug in this query key. The new useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys implementation fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions contains no organization identity. Two organizations with identical filters (particularly the default all-project selection) therefore share this cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attribute names, and concurrently mounted consumers can reuse a request for the wrong organization. Preserve the organization-specific cache identity that the previous endpoint-based key provided.

Include the organization slug or ID in this query key. The query function fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but the key contains only query options. Two organizations with the same project selection (especially the all-projects selection), date range and dataset therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attributes, and overlapping requests can populate the shared entry with the wrong organization's result.

issues.descricao: The UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps doc says only LOGS is supported, although the hooks are also used with SPANS.

comentarios.texto: The new shared prop documentation claims the endpoint currently supports only LOGS, but this PR also uses these hooks with TraceItemDataset.SPANS (for example in TransactionNameSearchBar). Update this comment to describe both supported datasets; as written it incorrectly tells callers that a supported and actively used input is unsupported.

issues.descricao: Error event timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay recording event timestamps (milliseconds), so errors are not interleaved chronologically with breadcrumbs.
dedupedYAxes is now just [yAxis], so its name misdescribes the code.

Every paginated breadcrumb-summary request queries the replay and fetches all of its error events from nodestore with no cap, adding latency and memory proportional to the replay's error count on each page.
HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES is applied only when a search query is present; the no-search early return shows all attributes, so the hidden attributes still appear in the default span attributes view.

The bulk delete test sets max_segment_id to None to cover the new guard in _make_recording_filenames, but it mocks delete_matched_rows, so the guard is never executed and removing it would not fail the test.
BrowserReportSerializer's validate_timestamp/validate_age docstrings claim one of age/timestamp must be present, but the code only enforces mutual exclusion, so reports with neither are accepted.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: PropertyResourceBundle is constructed from an InputStream, which the JDK reads as ISO-8859-1. WHY: Keycloak message files are UTF-8 encoded, so non-ASCII characters are mis-decoded before HTML and anchor checks, causing false positives/negatives in the sanitizer validation. HOW: Use new PropertyResourceBundle(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8) at lines 68 and 77.

WHAT: The Lithuanian totpStep1 message was replaced with Italian text. WHY: Users with Lithuanian locale will see an instruction in the wrong language, breaking the TOTP setup flow. HOW: Restore the correct Lithuanian translation for totpStep1.

WHAT: The Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 message was replaced with Italian text. WHY: Lithuanian-speaking users on the login TOTP page will see an instruction in the wrong language. HOW: Restore the correct Lithuanian translation for loginTotpStep1.

WHAT: The Simplified-Chinese (zh_CN) account totpStep1 message was replaced with Traditional-Chinese characters. WHY: Users selecting Simplified Chinese will see Traditional characters, which is inconsistent with the locale and with the rest of the file. HOW: Use Simplified Chinese equivalents: 手机, 安装, 应用程序.

issues.textoGolden: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).

comentarios.texto: The Lithuanian OTP setup instruction has been replaced with an Italian sentence. login-config-totp.ftl renders this message directly, so users selecting Lithuanian receive an instruction in the wrong language; the same copied sentence also appears in the Lithuanian account bundle at line 101. Replace both values with the Lithuanian translation of the new installation instruction.

The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian (“Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare”), but this is the Lithuanian locale and the surrounding setup steps are Lithuanian. Translate the new instruction into Lithuanian rather than copying the Italian translation. The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian, not Lithuanian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`). The same replacement was made for `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle. Compare the unchanged neighbouring lines (e.g. '打开应用扫描二维码…') which use Simplified forms; 手機/應用程式/安裝 are Traditional. zh_CN must be Simplified Chinese, so this string is in the wrong script/variant for the locale.

issues.textoGolden: Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

issues.descricao: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

comentarios.texto: The common prefix (start) and common suffix (end) are computed independently and can overlap, for example value "aa" vs sanitized "a". Then substring(start, length - end) gets begin > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan so that start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length()), e.g. `while (end < min - start && ...)`.

The common prefix and common suffix are computed independently and can overlap, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` can have start > end and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This crashes the verifier instead of reporting 'Illegal HTML'. Cap the suffix scan with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

WHAT: Common prefix/suffix stripping for the diff message can compute start+end larger than the string length and call substring(start, length-end) with start > end. WHY: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the key loop and crashes verification instead of reporting Illegal HTML. HOW: Clamp end so start+end <= min lengths, e.g. stop suffix scan when end >= length-start.

issues.descricao: normalizeValue blanks the entire choice expression for some keys before HTML validation, so markup placed inside a choice branch of those keys bypasses the new verifier.

comentarios.texto: Choice normalization removes all branch content before HTML validation, allowing prohibited markup to bypass the new translation policy. A translated error-invalid-multivalued-size value such as `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1

WHAT: normalizeValue replaces the entire {n,choice,...} block with ... before sanitizing, so HTML inside choice options is never checked. WHY: A translation can smuggle tags (e.g. {2,choice,0#<script>...}) in error-invalid-multivalued-size/linkExpirationFormatter keys and pass the verifier, reaching UI rendering as XSS. HOW: Sanitize/validate the choice body instead of blanking it, or run the HTML policy on the inner choice text as well.

issues.descricao: The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

comentarios.texto: The admin-ui bundle is consumed by react-i18next, which interpolates with double-brace `{{0}}` syntax (the previous value was `Attribute {{0}} ... {{2}}`). This line was rewritten to Java MessageFormat/ICU syntax (`{0}` ... `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), which i18next does not understand: the placeholders will not be substituted and the literal `{2,choice,...}` text will be shown to users. Keep the JS-side value in `{{0}}` form (and don't introduce ICU ChoiceFormat into the JS bundle); the ICU/choice spelling belongs only in the Java theme properties.

Same contract break in the account-ui bundle: the value was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` (i18next double-brace interpolation) and was changed to `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` MessageFormat+ICU syntax. The account console's i18next based consumer was not updated to match, so interpolation will fail and the raw placeholder/choice syntax will be rendered. Restore `{{0}}`-style placeholders for the JS bundle.

The account-ui bundle is consumed by i18next, which interpolates with double braces (the original string was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`). This PR aligned the value to the Java theme convention, replacing `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` with `{0}/{1}/{2}` and adding ICU `{2,choice,...}`. i18next will no longer substitute the placeholders and cannot interpret the ICU choice, so the account UI shows the raw `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and literal choice text. Keep the JS-side double-brace form for this bundle (adapt the choice accordingly) rather than the Java single-brace/ICU form used by the theme messages.

issues.descricao: If the English counterpart of a messages_*.properties file does not exist, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException that escapes the mojo, crashing the build instead of reporting a validation message.
The theme verifier's HTML and anchor regexes are case-sensitive, so uppercase tags in translations are flagged as illegal HTML by the build.

The anchor regex </?a[^>]*> in the theme verifier treats any tag starting with 'a' (<abbr>, <area>, ...) as an anchor tag, which can produce misleading anchor errors or strip such tags before HTML sanitizing.
The anchor-mismatch error in VerifyMessageProperties omits the message key and file, so the failing translation is hard to locate, unlike the 'Illegal HTML' message.

sugestoes.texto: The GrafanaRuleListItem rendered inside rules.map lacks a React key. React will fall back to array indices, which can cause incorrect reconciliation, stale state, and skipped re-renders when the filtered list changes. Add the existing key variable to the element.

AlertRuleMenu allows canSilence to be true from promRule-based abilities in the alert list view, but the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is only rendered when the optional RulerRuleDTO satisfies rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule. GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule, so rule is undefined and clicking Silence sets showSilenceDrawer without ever opening the drawer. Render the drawer from promRule when rule is absent, or gate the Silence menu item on having the data the drawer needs.

WHAT: RuleActionsButtons.V2 passes `rulerRule={rule}` where `rule` is undefined in the alert list view, but AlertRuleMenu only renders the Delete menu item when `canDelete && rulerRule` is truthy. WHY: Even when the user has delete permission and the delete flow works with the promRule-derived GrafanaRuleIdentifier, the Delete action is hidden for every Grafana rule rendered from the list view. HOW: Remove the `rulerRule` gate from the Delete menu item in AlertRuleMenu (the parent already guards non-V2 callers), or have V2 pass a delete-ability flag that does not depend on the ruler DTO.

WHAT: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` predicates Update, Delete, Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently on `isAlertingRule`, which is false for Grafana-managed recording rules. WHY: The previous `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` used `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` (true for both alerting and recording Grafana rules), so recording rules lose edit, delete, export and pause actions in the alert list view. HOW: Use `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule` (or `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`) for actions that apply to all Grafana-managed rules, keeping `isAlertingRule` only for actions that are genuinely alerting-only such as Silence.

issues.descricao: The pause menu item is still gated on a Grafana ruler rule, but the list view now passes only the Prometheus rule, so Pause/Resume disappears for list-view rules even when the user may pause them.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based pause ability cannot display Pause or Resume for list-view rules because the menu still requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) before rendering MenuItemPauseRule. GrafanaRuleListItem now supplies only promRule, so these actions disappear even for editable rules. Adapt the pause menu item to accept the Grafana identifier and Prometheus pause state, or load the ruler rule on demand.

issues.descricao: The Delete menu item still requires a ruler rule, which list-view Grafana rules no longer provide, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action.

comentarios.texto: The new Prometheus-based delete ability is still gated by `canDelete && rulerRule` when rendering the Delete item. Both Grafana list-view paths now omit rulerRule, so users with delete permission lose the Delete action entirely. Render deletion using the available identifier and group identifier instead of requiring the ruler DTO, adapting the callback contract accordingly.

issues.descricao: When the Grafana prom-rule branch is skipped (datasource rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) still reports Duplicate as supported and allowed by Grafana create permission, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler ability, so Duplicate appears on cloud rules even when the ruler check denies it.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: canDuplicate ORs ruler ability with grafana ability where grafana path is skipToken=>undefined for cloud rules, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) returns Duplicate=[true,true] whenever the user has global Grafana create permission. WHY: Any user with Grafana rule-create gets Duplicate menu item on cloud/Mimir rules even when ruler abilities deny it — incorrect authorization gating. HOW: Return NotSupported for all abilities when rule is skipToken/undefined, or gate grafana branch on prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) before ORing.

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities returns AlwaysSupported for Duplicate when rule is undefined (skipToken): loading is false from the !rule early-return, so MaybeSupported=true and duplicateSupported=true. ORed in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons this leaks Grafana create permission into non-Grafana rules. Gate MaybeSupported/duplicateSupported on rule existence (e.g. NotSupported when !rule).

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities must return NotSupported for all actions when rule is undefined (skipToken). Currently MaybeSupported falls back to AlwaysSupported when !loading, so Duplicate=[true, global-create] is true for a cloud rule passed as skipToken, and AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons OR-logic then incorrectly enables Duplicate (and Explore). Guard with if (!rule) return all-NotSupported abilities or make MaybeSupported require rule.

issues.descricao: The refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities into useAllRulerRuleAbilities drops the isFederatedRuleGroup check (isFederated is hardcoded false), so federated Mimir rules are reported as editable and deletable.

comentarios.texto: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false. The previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check is gone, so federated Mimir rules are no longer treated as immutable and can show edit and delete abilities. Keep the federation check in this wrapper, or pass the federation state into the shared hook.

Delegating useAllAlertRuleAbilities to useAllRulerRuleAbilities discards the group's federation status and replaces the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check with a constant false. Legacy RuleActionsButtons consequently enables editing rules in groups with source_tenants, although these groups were explicitly immutable before this change. Preserve the CombinedRule federation check in the wrapper or pass federation status into the delegated ability calculation.

Preserve the federated-group immutability check when delegating this CombinedRule hook. Previously useAllAlertRuleAbilities inspected rule.group with isFederatedRuleGroup and disabled modification/removal for federated rules. The replacement delegates to a hook that hardcodes isFederated=false and receives no group information. Existing useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities consumers therefore now receive supported update/delete abilities for federated rules when datasource permissions allow them, exposing operations that the previous contract explicitly prohibited. Pass the federation state through or retain that restriction in this wrapper.

issues.descricao: The Grafana prom-rule abilities gate Pause, Restore, Export and DeletePermanently on alertingRule(rule) while the comment claims it checks Grafana-managed rules, so Grafana recording rules lose these actions in the list view.

comentarios.texto: The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the variable it describes is `isAlertingRule`. That variable is true only for alerting rules and false for Grafana recording rules. Fix the comment, or rename the variable, so it says the check is for alerting rules. As written, readers will expect Pause, Export and Silence to be enabled for recording rules.

The comment says all GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed, but the check used is alertingRule(rule), which is false for recording rules. Pause, Restore, ModifyExport and DeletePermanently are therefore wrongly disabled for Grafana recording rules, where the old isGrafanaManagedAlertRule check allowed them. Use prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) for these abilities, and keep alertingRule only for Silence.

issues.descricao: The comment claims GrafanaPromRuleDTO abilities have no loading state, but the next line makes support depend on the folder loading flag.

comentarios.texto: The comment says there is no loading state, but the next line is `loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`. `loading` comes from the folder fetch. Update the comment to say that support depends on the folder loading state.

issues.descricao: The Grafana branch of the filtered rule list renders GrafanaRuleListItem without a key prop, so React reconciles the streaming list by index and warns about missing keys.
issues.textoGolden: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The grafana branch of the filtered list renders <GrafanaRuleListItem .../> without a `key` prop, dropping the `key={key}` that the replaced <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../> had. WHY: `rules.map` renders a dynamic list keyed by getRuleKey/hashRule; without a key React logs duplicate-key warnings and reconciles rows by index, so as the async rule stream updates/reorders the wrong rule row can be reused/mutated (stale state, swapped actions). HOW: add `key={key}` (the value is already destructured on line 152) to the <GrafanaRuleListItem> element.

WHAT: Grafana branch of FilterViewResults renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while datasource and unknown branches pass key. WHY: Breaks React list reconciliation — wrong item reuse, stale actions/state and console key warnings for every Grafana hit. HOW: Add key={key} to the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

issues.descricao: The test named 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks the More button exists, never the menu options.

comentarios.texto: The test 'should render More button with action menu options' only checks that the More button exists. It finds the button by name 'More', so the aria-label and text assertions are tautological. It would pass even if the menu had no actions or the abilities were broken. Click the button and assert the expected menu items, or rename the test to match what it checks.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never verifies any action menu option: the body only asserts the More button exists and has aria-label/text 'More'. It would still pass if the dropdown were rendered empty (Silence/Duplicate/Copy link/Export all missing), i.e. the behaviour the name promises is not covered. Either open the menu and assert the menu items, or rename the test to reflect that it only checks the trigger button's rendering/accessibility.

Test named 'should render More button with action menu options' never opens the menu nor asserts menu items — it only checks More button presence/aria/text. Click More and assert expected menuitems (or rename to 'should render More button') so it fails if menu actions break.

issues.descricao: GrafanaGroupLoader's JSDoc still says it loads from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints after the ruler query was removed.

comentarios.texto: The JSDoc for GrafanaGroupLoader still says "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints." but this PR removed the ruler API query entirely — the component now only calls useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery (Prometheus). The documentation describes a data source the function no longer consumes; update it to state only the Prometheus endpoint is loaded (and the same stale "Ruler response" reference in the expectedRulesCount prop doc at lines 18–19 should be corrected).

issues.descricao: For list-view Grafana rules RuleActionsButtons gets only promRule, so the Silence menu item is shown but the silence drawer, still gated on a ruler alerting rule, never renders and clicking Silence does nothing.
issues.textoGolden: RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

comentarios.texto: Passing only promRule enables the Silence notifications menu item but leaves RuleActionsButtons.V2 unable to render its silence drawer, which is guarded by rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). Clicking Silence only updates showSilenceDrawer and displays nothing because rule is undefined. Update the drawer to accept a rule UID—the inspected SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only needs grafana_alert.uid—and allow the Prometheus alerting-rule path to render it.

The new list item passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, but that component renders SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer only under `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. With rule undefined, clicking the newly enabled 'Silence notifications' action only sets state and never opens a drawer. Adapt the silence rendering path to load/use the rule by its Prometheus identifier before switching this caller to promRule-only.

WHAT: getEditableIdentifier now enables a prom-only path (Grafana uid identifier with rulerRule undefined) but the silence drawer still renders only when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. WHY: In the list view Silence menu item can be shown via grafana abilities, clicking it sets showSilenceDrawer but the drawer never mounts, so Silence silently does nothing. HOW: Gate the drawer on promRule as well or provide a prom-based silence drawer.

issues.descricao: RulesTable RBAC tests only mock useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and leave useRulerRuleAbilities denied, so the ruler-based Delete permission branch of AlertRuleMenu is never tested.
A stray '// duplicate' comment was left next to useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule) in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The write lock is acquired unconditionally and the cache is not re-checked after locking, so every request in Dev mode and all concurrent first requests in production serialize and redundantly read assets-manifest.json. WHY: This blocks the index handler, frontend settings API, and panic recovery middleware on a global lock during file I/O, causing a material startup/request slowdown in a hot path. HOW: Add a double-checked read after acquiring the write lock so that only the first production caller loads the manifest; for Dev mode, skip the cache lock entirely or read without caching since the cached value is never used there.

WHAT: Every GetWebAssets call takes an exclusive write lock and recomputes web assets without re-checking the cache after locking. WHY: In Dev mode this serializes all page requests behind a single lock, and in non-Dev mode a cold-start stampede repeats the same manifest read multiple times. HOW: Re-check entryPointAssetsCache under the write lock before recomputing, and skip the lock/cache write entirely in Dev mode to preserve the prior Dev behavior.

WHAT: Every GetWebAssets call takes an exclusive write lock and recomputes web assets without re-checking the cache after locking. WHY: In Dev mode this serializes all page requests behind a single lock, and in non-Dev mode a cold-start stampede repeats the same manifest read multiple times. HOW: Re-check entryPointAssetsCache under the write lock before recomputing, and skip the lock/cache write entirely in Dev mode to preserve the prior Dev behavior.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent callers that missed the cache each reload the assets manifest.
issues.textoGolden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. WHY: On a cold cache, all concurrent callers (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) block on the write lock and then each sequentially re-executes the full load (file I/O or blocking http.DefaultClient.Do), producing a thundering-herd serialization and N redundant loads instead of one; in Dev mode this happens on every request since the fast path is skipped, serializing all concurrent page loads. HOW: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so only the first goroutine performs the load, and drop the defer in favor of releasing the lock immediately after assigning `entryPointAssetsCache = result` to avoid holding it during I/O.
cache is not re-checked under the lock after re-acquiring write Lock, so concurrent callers can each recompute web assets

The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets holds a global exclusive mutex through the whole manifest load, so in Dev mode, where the cache is bypassed, every request serializes behind it.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice with incompatible signatures, so the second definition silently replaces the first. WHY: The existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 invokes the old 5-argument form (path, path, 100, 100, opts), but the surviving method accepts only 3-4 arguments, causing an ArgumentError and breaking emoji resizing. HOW: Remove the duplicate definition at lines 149-151 and update resize_emoji.rb to pass a dimensions string, e.g., OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, '100x100', opts).

WHAT: OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice with incompatible signatures, so the second definition replaces the first at class-load time. WHY: Jobs::ResizeEmoji still calls the original four-argument form (downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)), which will raise ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4) and break emoji resizing. HOW: Keep a single downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) signature and update the ResizeEmoji caller to pass "100x100" as the dimensions string.

issues.descricao: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.
issues.textoGolden: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: A second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined that overrides the existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at lines 145-147. WHY: Ruby uses the last definition, so the effective downsize now only accepts 3-4 args, and the existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) passes 5 args and raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4), breaking emoji resizing. HOW: Remove the duplicate; keep a single downsize method whose signature matches all callers (the 4-arg uploads_controller call `downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` and the 5-arg ResizeEmoji call), or rename one of them.

`downsize` is defined twice: the original 5-param form `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at lines 145-147 and the new 4-param form `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at lines 149-151. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the effective signature is now 4 params and the 5-param version is dead code. The pre-existing consumer app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 positional args, which now raises ArgumentError on every emoji resize. Either update that caller to the new `dimensions` form or remove the redundant override so the old signature keeps working.

`self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class scope (line 145 `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and the new line 149 `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`). Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the 4-argument version is dead and unreachable. The existing caller `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 passes 5 arguments and will now raise ArgumentError (expected 3..4). Remove the duplicate definition (keep only the `dimensions`-based one, or convert resize_emoji's call), otherwise emoji resizing breaks.

issues.descricao: The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

comentarios.texto: Hardcoded max size literal 10 * 1024 replaces site-setting-derived max size. Behavioral concern outside assigned class.

The fixed 10 MB client limit is applied to attachments as well as images, replacing max_attachment_size_kb. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload those valid files through the composer, although UploadValidator still permits them. Apply the new input ceiling only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

WHAT: Client check hardcodes maxSizeKB to 10*1024 instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'], losing image vs attachment distinction. WHY: Sites with smaller max_attachment_size_kb pass client validation then fail server-side, and sites with limits >10MB incorrectly block valid uploads with wrong max_size_kb message. HOW: Restore per-type SiteSetting lookup (keep 10MB only as image downsize ceiling).

issues.descricao: The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
issues.textoGolden: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

comentarios.texto: The controller passes the percentage string `"80%"` as the dimensions argument to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but the consumer requires explicit `WxH` geometry: the code this PR deleted built exactly `"#{width}x#{height}"`, and the animated path runs `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`, which rejects a percentage. Pass an explicit size (e.g. a computed `"WxH"` from the max KB target) so the auto-downsize actually reduces the file, rather than silently no-oping and leaving oversized uploads.

Caller passes "80%" as dimensions to OptimizedImage.downsize, but the downsize/optimize instruction builders in optimized_image.rb expect explicit "WxH" geometry (interpolated as -resize #{dimensions}\>). A bare percentage does not satisfy that contract and will produce a malformed geometry. Fix the caller to supply WxH dimensions or add explicit percentage handling to the callee.

issues.descricao: Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new auto-downsize call passes a tempfile path whose name has no `.GIF` extension, so `optimize` never selects the animated branch (`method_name += "_animated" if opts[:allow_animation] && from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) and uses `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert from[0]` and keeps only the first frame. WHY: Animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb that are uploaded through this path have their animation flattened to a single frame even though SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. HOW: Detect the image type from the original filename/content-type rather than the tempfile path (or pass a flag) so the gifsicle animated downsize path is used for GIF inputs.

Passing the multipart tempfile path to downsize prevents animation detection when that path does not end in .gif, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. OptimizedImage.optimize checks the path suffix and otherwise uses convert with input[0], so oversized animated GIF uploads are permanently flattened to their first frame. Preserve the original image extension in the processing path or pass the image format explicitly to select animated processing.

issues.descricao: The comment promises images are reduced to the allowed size, but the loop only tries five 80% reductions with no guarantee of reaching the limit.

comentarios.texto: The comment says large images are "automatically reduced to allowed size", but the loop only resizes by 80% up to 5 attempts (≈0.33× of the original in the best case) and then stops without any check that the result actually meets `max_image_size_kb`. The prose promises a guarantee the code does not provide; either make the loop actually converge to the allowed size or reword the comment to state that the image is only attempted to be reduced.

issues.descricao: The downsize retry loop ignores the false return of a failed conversion and repeats the same failing ImageMagick call up to five times.

comentarios.texto: The retry loop ignores downsize's false return value and retries failed conversions while the file remains oversized. convert_with returns false on converter failure, so an unsupported or malformed oversized image launches the same failing external conversion up to five times per upload without any changed input. Break on a failed downsize result and return an upload error rather than repeating the conversion.

WHAT: Downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize return value and retries up to 5 times unconditionally while checking tempfile.size. WHY: Failed converts (e.g. SVG, invalid 80%> geometry, corrupt image) burn 5 ImageMagick runs then Upload.create_for still runs with oversized/unmodified file and fails validation, wasting CPU and breaking the feature. HOW: Break on false return and handle failure.

issues.descricao: Claims up to five synchronous ImageMagick runs per oversized upload block request threads and enable DoS.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Up to 5 synchronous OptimizedImage.downsize + ImageOptim convert runs execute inline in create_upload request cycle for every oversized image. WHY: Blocks the Rails request thread with CPU-intensive shell-outs per upload, enabling easy request-thread exhaustion/DoS with large images. HOW: Move downsizing to background job or enforce single-pass/timeout.

issues.descricao: Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
issues.textoGolden: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

issues.descricao: The 413 upload error message states a hard-coded 10 MB maximum that may not match the limit the server or web server actually enforces.

The upload tempfile path, which for API URL uploads embeds the request-controlled type param, is now passed to OptimizedImage.downsize and run unescaped in a shell via backticks, allowing command injection through type.
Oversized SVG uploads go through the new ImageMagick downsize loop because SVG counts as an image, so the vector file is rasterized or corrupted in place before Upload.create_for parses it as SVG.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource created via from_integration carries the same import-time timestamp. WHY: The `queued` field cannot fulfill its intended purpose of recording when the assignment was queued, which will mislead any future logging, metrics, or TTL logic that relies on it. HOW: Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance gets the current time at creation.

issues.descricao: AssignmentSource.queued defaults to timezone.now() evaluated at class definition, so all instances share the import-time timestamp instead of the time they were queued.
issues.textoGolden: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates once at class-definition time so every AssignmentSource without explicit queued shares the same timestamp. WHY: queued time is wrong/stale for all later instances and defeats its purpose as a queue-time marker. HOW: use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` (with `field` import).

Field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import so all AssignmentSources share the same timestamp. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance measures its actual creation/queue time.

The dataclass field default `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the module is imported, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit `queued` value (which is exactly what `from_integration` does, and what `from_dict` falls back to when the key is absent) shares the same frozen import-time timestamp instead of the moment the assignment was actually queued. This makes the `queued` timestamp semantically wrong/meaningless (it reflects process start, not assignment time) and would silently misreport the queue time anywhere this value is later inspected. Fix by defaulting in a factory/`__post_init__` or making the caller pass the timestamp, e.g. set `queued` inside `from_integration` (`queued=timezone.now()`), or use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

issues.descricao: The test method name test_from_dict_inalid_data has a typo; it should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
issues.textoGolden: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.

comentarios.texto: Typo in test name test_from_dict_inalid_data hides it from name-filtered runs (e.g. -k invalid_data): fix spelling to test_from_dict_invalid_data so the invalid-payload guard is actually selected and verified.

issues.descricao: test_from_dict_empty_array actually passes an empty dict, so the name does not match what the test exercises.
issues.textoGolden: Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

comentarios.texto: The test is named test_from_dict_empty_array but it passes an empty dict ({}), not an empty array; a caller reading the name will believe the empty-list/array input path is covered when it is not. Rename it to test_from_dict_empty_dict (or pass [] to actually cover the empty-array case) so the identifier agrees with the input it exercises.

test_from_dict_empty_array names an empty array but constructs an empty dict (`data: dict[str, Any] = {}`), so it only re-exercises the empty/None path and never covers empty-array input; a regression specific to that input would pass unnoticed. Pass a real empty array or rename the test to match its body.

test_from_dict_empty_array passes {} rather than an empty array. It therefore only tests missing required dictionary keys and would still pass if rejection of an array input were broken. Pass [] to exercise the named case (or rename this test to empty_dict if that is the intended contract).

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context builds a modified copy of the monitor config but returns the original unmodified config. WHY: The schedule_type display-name translation is computed on the copy and discarded, so issue occurrences report the raw schedule_type integer instead of the human-readable name. HOW: Return "config": config instead of "config": monitor_environment.monitor.config.

issues.descricao: get_failure_reason's docstring examples do not match the strings the function returns.

comentarios.texto: The `get_failure_reason` docstring describes output this function does not produce. The singular branch (line 146) returns a `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP` value such as "A missed check-in was detected", yet the docstring advertises "A failed check-in was detected"; the multi-check-in branch joins `"%(count)d %(status)s"` fragments with `get_text_list(..., last_word=_("and"))` and appends " check-ins detected", yielding "2 missed and 1 error check-ins detected", not the docstring's "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". Update the examples (or the format string) so the documented contract matches the code.

The get_failure_reason docstring examples don't match the output. It shows 'A failed check-in was detected' and '...were detected', but the code returns the per-status singular strings ('A missed check-in was detected') or '<list> check-ins detected'. Update the examples to the real output and fix the 'humam readible' typo.

issues.descricao: get_monitor_environment_context builds a config copy with the human-readable schedule_type but returns the original monitor.config, so the conversion is lost and the context shows the raw value.
issues.textoGolden: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config to `config` and converts schedule_type display, but returns the original monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of `config`. WHY: the display conversion never takes effect so the occurrence context carries the raw schedule_type value, producing wrong output vs the function's evident intent. HOW: return `"config": config` instead of `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config`.

Dead computation: `config` is copied and `config['schedule_type']` transformed to display value, but return uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (original) instead of `config`. Change to `"config": config` so transformation is used.

WHAT: In get_monitor_environment_context the code copies config and replaces config['schedule_type'] with the human-readable get_schedule_type_display(), but the returned context dict uses the original `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified local `config`, so the mutation is dead. WHY: The occurrence's monitor context always reports the raw schedule_type value rather than the display string the code intended to substitute, producing incorrect evidence data in the emitted occurrence. HOW: return the local variable, i.e. use "config": config in the returned dict.
